COJ Billing Blunders UPDATE

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The City of Johannesburg keeps making promises to sort out the decade-long billing crisis, but is anything changing?

Unique Selling Point:
In May, MMC for Finance, Rabelani Dagada made on-screen promises to the Carte Blanche viewers about sorting out the billing crisis in the city. Three months later we revisit the cases to see nothing much has changed, despite Mayor Herman Mashaba's recent drive to solve the crisis once and for all.

Summary:
We revisit the case studies from Billing Blunders, who will all say the same thing... Their cases, which MMC Dagada undertook to solve personally are still in exactly the same situation. Carlos Siemos has had 2x pre-termination notices since our last broadcast and no joy in having his account fixed. He is being billed for the wrong meter (has been for the past 5 years). Soso Gwadiso is still fighting with the council to get his money refunded that his wife paid to get his electricity reconnected. Mike Lingwood's account keeps escalating despite the fact that we dug the meter up in May, which indicates the account reading is completely inaccurate. Mike is also struggling to get the COJ to write off some prescribed debt which dates back to the previous owner of the building. MMC Dagada promised this issue will be sorted by August. No joy there either.

Despite numerous phone calls and emails and follow-ups on my part, the only intervention came when I contacted Mayor Mashaba himself, then all of a sudden the Van Niekerk's electricity was switched back on at 10pm on a Friday evening. Their water was reconnected the following week. Yet, their account is still in the name of the deceased mother which means that soon they will once again be disconnected since the account is in arrears. This account needs to be written off against the mother's estate and the Van Niekerk's need to be allowed to open their own water and electricity account with COJ. Despite having presented their mother's death certificate on various occasions and many letter and trips to the ombudsman, they are still struggling.

Further information:
Mayor Herrman Mashaba has recently made numerous public statements regarding the billing crisis and how he personally is getting involved. The COJ are setting up various special "Billing Open Days" where members of the public can raise queries. And while they all arrive with bells and whistles, there is an element of concern that how are they able to solve thousands of queries when they cannot even solve the 5 issues we presented them with in May.

Press Release:


COJ Billing Blunders II
For years, the City of Johannesburg’s rates, water and electricity billing system has been in absolute chaos. Residents
were frustrated by exaggerated estimates, incorrect readings and system errors but three months ago, the
municipality - under a new local government - promised that it would finally resolve the City's outstanding billing
issues. Carte Blanche returns to examine whether those promises have been fulfilled.

Script:


COJ Billing Blunders Update
V/o
It's end of the month and time to pay the bills, but one account in particular has been a headache for many city residents...
LINK
The so-called Joburg Billing crisis has been around for more than a decade... and sorting the mess out is a particular thorn in the flesh of the DA Administration.
V/o
Executive Mayor Herman Mashaba says they've made a lot of progress.
Mashaba
When we took over this administration last year we discovered there were over 100,000 of cases of our billing being a challenge. Lucky enough we're sitting right now just under 15,000...
V/o
Three months ago we reported on the state of the City's revenue department and highlighted the plight of a few residents who have been struggling for some time to sort out their City Of Joburg accounts.
V/o
One of our Case studies was Jan & Bertha van Niekerk, two SASSA pensioners who live in their diseased mother's house on the Southern side of the city. At the time they had already been living without electricity for over a year and their water had been cut too.

UPSOUND

The problem was that the account was still in the name of the Bertha's late mother and despite numerous efforts to close the account they had no luck.
V/o
At the time we spoke to the City's MMC of Finance, Dr Rabelani Dagada and he made a string of promises.
RECAP
Bongani: Can you at least promise us, here and now, on the record that at least the people that we have used to highlight these problems, you will sort it out?

MMC Dagada: Uhm, I'm promising i'm going to attend to those queries personally. I'll deal with them.

V/o
In July, six weeks after our broadcast, Jan & Berthas water was reconnected. Around the same time the City of Joburg also came to reconnect their electricity.
Jan van Niekerk
Hulle het gekom die Vrydag en dit aangesit, en die Maandag more weer gesny.
V/o
And then the power was reconnected for a second time on Thursday this week, three hours after our meeting with MMC Dagada.

But the actual problem remains unresolved and by next week, they may very well be disconnected again...
Dagada
I'll be honest with you....if I as the MMC starts to focus on particular individual consumers I won't be able to do this job properly.

Derek: You made a promise to carte Blanche that you would sort out those queries personally and it hasn't happened.

Dagada: We've gone a long way to get most of those resolved.

Derek: Not according to all of the case studies that we've spoken to.

Dagada: But as I said. Each query has certain circumstances. The problem we're making here is that we're assuming that the City is always at the wrong, which is not the situation. So, if somebody is genuinely owing the city they may as well even spend three years without electricity.
V/o
Soso Gwadiso was another one of our case studies in May. At the time he was in dispute with the City over estimated readings dating back to when he bought his house. This query too has not been resolved.
Soso
I've been to Thuso house, I have been to the office downtown to try get assistance. I'm still sitting in the same position.
V/o
Property redeveloper Michael Lingwood owns this building in Berea. In May his account was over R7 million, and it keeps growing every month.
Michael Lingwood
We are still getting a R50,000 account for water whilst no water is entering this property at all, whatsoever, for the past 14 years.
V/o
Michael also spends a lot his time assisting other Joburg residents with their incorrect accounts, like Mrs Kwan.

She owns a few properties in downtown Johannesburg and out of fear of victimisation chose not to appear on camera –

UPSOUND
All my life since I got these buildings I thought it can be my pension but I think it turned out to be a nightmare

but Michael was keen to show us some of her issues with the city of Johannesburg.
Mrs Kwan
.
V/o
This residential building has had no water, nor a water meter, for more than 3 years, yet she is billed monthly.
Michael Lingwood
They are saying here that you are using R1568 worth of water.
V/o
She showed us 2 other properties with similar issues. No water meters and yet the accounts keep coming...
UPSOUND Mike & Mrs Kwan
You are still owing them R354,000.

Yes

Despite there being absolutely no water to this property?

Yes
V/o
And if this is not enough, she also took us to two separate premises with prepaid meters, and yet the City still charges her for electricity every month.
V/o
Business owner Glen Brits is also being charged despite the fact that he's had prepaid electricity since February this year. And his account states that the charges are based on ACTUAL readings.
Glen Brits
This is a prepaid meter and yet the council is charging us as well. How can they give us an actual reading if we've basically got prepaid?
V/o
In our May Broadcast Michael also raised the issue of prescribed debt.
Mike




Bongani: So by when will the prescribed debts be off the books? 

MMC Dagada: By end of August, by end of August. August this year 
V/o
Now MMC Dagada is satisfied that they delivered on this promise.
Dagada
I said to you by the end of August we would have written off all prescribed debt and we talked in May, and the end of June, 30th of June we wrote off around R2billion of prescribed debt.


v/o
Michael strongly disagrees.
Michael Lingwood
Over R2.1Billion worth of accounts still contain prescribed debt which is totally illegal and they are sending them out on a monthly basis.
V/o
Eloise Boesak has had a few run-ins with the City in the past few months.
Eloise Boesak
I'm really really angry. So frustrated by the lack of feedback and understanding around what is a basic basic issue. We got a bill out of nowhere for R28,000. And when we questioned it, having paid faithfully and analysed it, nobody could give us an explanation.
V/o
But as soon as that query was resolved she received another incoherent account for her main residence.
Eloise Boesak
So because we have engaged with the city before, what I did is I immediately contacted the lady who had helped us previously to state: Here's last months's bill, here's our actual proof of payment and here's this new bill. Can somebody please explain the gibberish to me because it does not make any logical sense. I did not get a response initially, and then for our joy three days later we got our first pre-termination notice. Today I drove up from work ready for this discussion with another pre-termination notice placed on my gate. That's 2 in three days.
V/o
In speaking to all these people it would seem like the City of Johannesburg's billing problem is growing, rather than shrinking...
Dagada
Uh, that is not true. What we have done as the new administration is that we became more transparent about it. We think the previous administration swept it under the carpet.
V/o
In the meantime, people like Jan & Bertha, Mrs Kwan and Eloise live in fear of disconnection and they can only hope that those in charge of the city will ultimately deliver on their promises...
Mashaba
I've said to a commitment to the people of Johannesburg. By December for me, if I don't really see a massive improvement I'm asking residents of the City of Johannesburg to fire me.




PROMO 10”

How much longer do Johannesburg residents have to struggle with their monthly utilities accounts? Is the end of the so-called billing crisis in sight?


PROMO 15”
Johannesburg residents are desperate for the City to sort out its billing problems

Eloise...


PROMO 15”
Trying to resolve City of Joburg billing queries is a huge headache for many residents..

Jan …

Can those in charge of the city deliver on their promises?
